stem: What is the usual epidemiological pattern of acute respiratory tract infections in paediatrics?

options.text: Usually chronic infections in adolescents during summer
Usually acute viral infections, most prevalent among young children and in winter
Usually bacterial infections, most prevalent among newborns and in summer
Usually fungal infections, most prevalent among school-aged children in spring
Usually parasitic infections with no age or seasonal pattern

explanation: Usually acute viral infections, most prevalent among young children and in winter. This is the characteristic epidemiological pattern of acute respiratory tract infections in paediatrics.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Respiratory 3.1 Acute Respiratory Problems

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because acute respiratory tract infections are typically acute, not chronic, and are most common in young children rather than adolescents in summer.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because acute respiratory tract infections in paediatrics are usually viral, occur most often in young children, and are more common in winter.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because these infections are not usually described as bacterial, and the typical age and seasonal pattern given is different.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fungal infection is not the usual pattern for paediatric acute respiratory tract infections, nor is this seasonal distribution described.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because acute respiratory tract infections do have a clear age and seasonal pattern, rather than no pattern at all.
